newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek PM's "new-look" cabinet has old faces.
newsitem.headline: Greek PM's "new-look" cabinet has old faces.

text.p: Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis kept the backbone of his economic team on Tuesday when he named his new socialist cabinet but chose a different defence minister to oversee plans to beef up the military.
Yannos Papandoniou, who drove down double-digit inflation, became the economic "czar", retaining his post as national economy minister as well as being given the finance ministry.
Simitis, fresh from a convincing national election win on Sunday, mixed old-guard socialists with the younger generation of reformers who helped put him in power.
"During the formation of this cabinet we sought to combine tested experience with the need for renewal," said acting Press Minister Dimitris Konstas.
Among his close colleagues, Simitis renamed Vasso Papandreou as the development minister despite her confrontations with foreign investors, especially over private casinos.
Theodoros Pangalos kept the foreign ministry. The blunt diplomat, whose outspoken criticism of EU partners has landed him in trouble in the past, has been on his best behaviour.
Simitis's boldest move was to remove Gerassimos Arsenis, an old-guard socialist, from the defence ministry and replace him with Akis Tsohatzopoulos.

Tsohatzopoulos opposed Simitis's rise to power after ailing party founder Andreas Papandreou resigned as prime minister in January. He challenged Simitis for the party leadership in June, and lost, but has since strongly supported the new premier.

Alexandros Papadopoulos, Greece's respected finance minister since 1993, replaced Tsohatzopoulos at the interior ministry. He has long wanted to leave the unpopular finance ministry, which oversees taxation and the budget.
George Papandreou, son and political heir of Andreas, took a step up and was named deputy foreign minister. He had been the education minister.

Papandreou gave an impassioned speech in support of Simitis during the brutal party leadership conference in June, earning a more prominent post, but he was considered too inexperienced to head the ministry.
